tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and had not plateaued; loss of this single gas export train would cut production within an hour.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist to analyze the spectrum and inspect the NDE bearing/rotor train; correct per findings and verify stable acceptable vibration after correction. Confirm current compressor capability. Diagnose the vibration mechanism. Obtain source-required attention today.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Bearing vibration more than doubled over six weeks, with a growing 1x component and sidebands, and the upward trend had not plateaued. Although still below alarm and without demonstrated function loss, this is strong progression supporting high near-term likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the single gas export compressor train has no spare or workaround; a trip sends the platform to recycle and cuts production within the hour. This is a severe operational consequence, but no extreme safety consequence is established.

tickets.summary: Below-set-pressure hissing and hydrocarbon odor indicate PSV-1310 is passing, impairing the sole V-1201 overpressure protection layer; relief capability and restoration remain unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Have pressure-systems authority diagnose leakage and disposition operation; repair as indicated, then pop/leak-test to certified set pressure and tightness. Check current leak and personnel exposure. Check impairment/deviation register. Confirm protection restored. Pop/leak-test after correction.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Below-set-pressure hissing and hydrocarbon odor are direct evidence of active passing or weeping, detected by ear and smell and expressly treated as protection impairment. Relief-on-demand capability was not tested, so complete protective-function loss is suspected rather than confirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the sole safety-critical PSV would remove V-1201 overpressure protection, creating severe major-accident exposure with no stated redundant relief device. The evidence supports the severe band but does not define consequences sufficiently for the extreme band.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first test start, then started after ~8 s; batteries were 22.8 V at rest and rated pressure was achieved, but dependable firewater demand start is impaired and FW-8101 capacity is unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire-protection authority to assess disposition; inspect batteries and starting air, then correct defects found. Check impairment/deviation register. Retest first-attempt start and rated pressure. Verify FW-8101 flow and pressure capacity.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: FW-8102 demonstrably failed its required first-attempt demand-start function during the weekly test. A successful second attempt after about eight seconds and normal running preserve delivery capability once started but do not negate the observed start failure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start removes one of two firewater pumps from dependable demand service. The linked pump started but later delivered 9.2 barg versus 11 barg with flow unmeasured, so its capacity cannot be credited as verified; complete firewater loss supports severe major-accident exposure and production shutdown.

tickets.summary: At the low-point drain, wet-insulation CUI reduced the 6-in full-pressure flowline to 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum; containment loss could release hydrocarbons, while adjacent windows were within tolerance.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to define isolation/repair, correct wall loss, and verify restored thickness and pressure integrity against approved criteria. Check inventory, ignition and personnel exposure. Confirm current containment and isolation. Map CUI extent around the low-point drain.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Wet-insulation corrosion has produced advanced localized wall loss: 6.2 mm is below the 7.4 mm minimum allowable. The active CUI mechanism and breached limit support high near-term concern, but no leak or failed containment test confirms loss of function.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the sole 6-inch production flowline pressure boundary could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure. This supports severe major-accident and personnel exposure, but the evidence does not define release magnitude or occupancy sufficiently for the extreme band.

tickets.summary: P-3305 tripped three times this month, making wellhead-manifold inhibitor injection intermittent for about 10 days; the suspected diaphragm fault risks downstream corrosion within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Corrosion engineer to assess and authorize repair; then verify approved discharge pressure/rate. Check downstream corrosion condition. Check impairment/deviation register. Confirm current continuous injection. Inspect diaphragm and pump internals.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The pump repeatedly interrupted continuous inhibitor delivery: three low-discharge-pressure trips in one month and intermittent injection for around ten days. The diaphragm is only a suspected cause, but required-function loss is observed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the sole corrosion-inhibitor pump does not stop production, but starvation initiates downstream carbon-steel corrosion within weeks and creates a delayed integrity consequence. No redundant pump is identified.

tickets.summary: V-1305's inlet deflector is partly detached after 1 of 4 brackets corroded through; shell and heads are sound, and the separator is out of service with indefinite bypass, limiting current impact but requiring repair before well testing.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to inspect remaining supports and approve repair or securement of the inlet deflector before return to service.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: One of four supports has corroded through and the deflector is partly detached, establishing meaningful degradation but not demonstrated loss of separation function. The sound shell and heads, out-of-service state, and supported bypass limit near-term progression exposure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the inlet-deflection function could compromise test-separator operation during well testing, but the separator can be isolated and bypassed indefinitely without production impact. This supports a localized, recoverable consequence.

tickets.summary: V-2450’s local level gauge is hard to read, but transmitter control appeared normal and no downstream carryover was indicated; loss of level awareness could allow turbine-damaging liquid carryover.
tickets.recommended_action: Clean the gauge glass; inspect for damage or fouling, correct as found, and confirm readable indication agrees with the transmitter. Compare gauge and transmitter to a reference.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The gauge was dirty and hard to read, demonstrating limited degradation but not confirmed inability to indicate level. No progression, glass damage, leakage, or abnormal process performance is reported, and V-2450 has a reliability score of 7.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the local gauge would degrade level awareness, but the reported transmitter path appeared to control normally. If scrubber level control were consequently lost, liquid carryover could damage turbines; the supported remaining indication limits this local gauge failure to a recoverable consequence.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the non-redundant, safety-critical pressure boundary for the entire first stage could cause severe loss-of-containment and major-accident exposure; the evidence does not define inventory or personnel exposure sufficiently to support the extreme band.
